:::{#def-positive-classification}
#### Positive classification

In a [binary classification problem](#def-binary-classification) with $\scrC = \set{k_1, k_0}$,
$k_1$ is called the **positive class**,
and for an observation drawn from a [population](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-population)
and assigned [class](#def-class) $Y \in \scrC$
(for example, $Y = c(X)$ when a [classification rule](#def-classification-rule) $c$ classifies the observation from its feature $X$),
a **positive classification**
(also called **positive**, and written $\posclass$)
is the [event](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-event)
that the observation is assigned to $k_1$:

$$\posclass \eqdef \set{Y = k_1}$$ {#eq-positive-classification}

Source: @wikipedia_statistical_classification;
@wikipedia_sensitivity_and_specificity.
:::
